paragraphs:
The first few days were the toughest. That empty silence in the house, that's probably the hardest part.

But I've found each day gets a little easier. I never thought on Day 1 that Day 28 would feel so normal. Yet here I am.

I don't know why I'm sharing this, but I guess I just needed to share that I'm doing okay, and if you've gone/are going through something similar, you'll be alright too in due time.

body.heading: I grew up with a severe learning disability/processing disorder. While I know how to code alright, the uphill battle that came with that education was grueling.

paragraphs: When people ask me to describe my learning disability I tell them

richText.text: When people ask me to describe my learning disability I tell them

paragraphs: "Where most peoples' brains work like an eight lane highway, my brain functions like it has only one lane."

paragraphs:
This makes things like instruction following, keeping track of things, etc. very difficult.
While I learned to work around it as an adult, it's still something that makes life more work for me than most.

paragraphs:
I was one of the first 100,000 people to try ChatGPT, and right away I knew it would change the world. I didn't know if it would be for better or for worse but I knew it would be something monumental.

Fast forward to 2026, and it's a part of my work and personal life in a way I never thought possible. Tasks that used to be more grueling for me than most, I can now condense into bite sized digestible information that's easy for me to comprehend.

paragraphs:
Creating software, big and small became far more feasible, and with AI I discovered a passion for creating human-instructed & fine-tuned software. I've always had the eye of an artist, even at a young age. My great-uncle was Jimmy Carter's photographer, and his father was FDR's, Truman's and Kennedy's. I believe because of those people, illustrating, writing and photography have always come naturally to me.

And despite being right-brained the same time I've always loved computers. In 2004, at a young age, I used to get up at 5:00 AM before school, sneak over to the family computer and log on to RuneScape which is where I learned to type.

Being able to describe exactly what I want, in plain English to a computer, and have it spit it out almost exactly how I want it with the ability to fine tune it to my preferences, has been one of the most liberating technological moments of my life.

paragraphs: Let me be clear, I don't believe AI generated imagery and videos should be considered art.

richText.text: Let me be clear, I don't believe AI generated imagery and videos should be considered art.

paragraphs:
I still create pixel art, draw, and photograph my work by hand, but when it comes to code, I find it miraculous being naturally able to converse with a machine, and it being able to understand exactly what I want in the only ways my broken brain knows how to convey it.

I know this stance may be considered controversial, as AI is a controversial tool. But for someone like me, it's a super power, that's helped me overcome a lifelong handicap.
